tasks.title: Establish executable quality harness
acceptanceCriteria: Repository exposes validate and status commands
Controller state and logs are persisted
A boundary check rejects UI/server imports from domain
tasks.notes: Plan: scaffold the executable TypeScript harness, prove the quality gate, then commit it before the first product slice. Verifier findings (2026-08-17): initial checker accepted an empty/missing domain directory and had no negative proof. Remediated with an actual domain module, explicit web/server/storage import detection, and temporary-fixture rejection tests. Post-remediation evidence: npm run validate passed on 2026-08-17 (format, typecheck, build, architecture check, 3 tests). Final verifier PASS after atomic state update. Independent verifier sandbox could not write dist/index.js (TS5033); that environment limitation was not reproduced by the controller validation. Controller evolution (2026-08-17): replaced the logging stub with a standalone Codex CLI loop, persisted active-state and blocker transitions, a bounded-run option, JSONL events, three-failure safety stop, and controller-state acceptance tests. No dependency added.

tasks.title: Create routines with deterministic scheduling
acceptanceCriteria: User can create a routine
Daily, weekly, monthly and interval schedules calculate next due dates
Calendar edge cases are tested
tasks.notes: Completed 2026-08-17. Domain slice: daily, weekly, monthly, and positive intervals; immutable completion; pause status; end-of-month and leap-year tests. Browser preview creates routines and displays domain-calculated dates. API tests cover success and invalid/unsupported schedules. Browser evidence: keyboard form navigation plus successful weekly creation of Wipe kitchen counter in Kitchen, displaying next due 2026-08-24, no console errors or failed network requests. Durable post-creation screenshots: `.agent/evidence/HR-002/desktop-routine-created.jpg` (1280x720) and `.agent/evidence/HR-002/mobile-routine-created-390x844.jpg` (390px viewport). Daily schedule correctly hides interval-only control. Harness audit: initial full-page screenshot timeout was retried using standard viewport captures, which succeeded. Fresh verifier PASS; full validation passed (13 tests).

tasks.title: Make Today and Upcoming routines useful
acceptanceCriteria: Today distinguishes due, upcoming, and paused routines
User can see at least the next due date and schedule context
Desktop and mobile hierarchy makes the next action clear
tasks.notes: Plan: replace the single-result preview with a persistent, status-grouped Today and Upcoming list; expose domain-derived status through the HTTP boundary; make paused routines reachable with a focused pause/resume control; prove domain/API behavior and capture desktop/mobile keyboard browser evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-17: the domain owns display-safe next-due/status views, the API returns them and supports pause/resume, and the UI groups Due now, Upcoming, and Paused routines with schedule context. Acceptance coverage: domain and API tests, including upcoming-before-pause and paused list states. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-003/desktop-all-groups-full.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-003/mobile-all-groups-full-390x844.png`, and `.agent/evidence/HR-003/browser-checks.json` show all groups, keyboard flows, visible values, console inspection, and successful POST/PATCH behavior. Fresh verifier PASS after evidence remediation; `npm run validate` passed (18 tests).

tasks.title: Complete due routines and surface recent history
acceptanceCriteria: A due routine can be marked complete from Today
Completion is recorded against the boundary's local date and changes the displayed next due date
The latest completion is visible in the routine's history context
tasks.notes: Plan: expose the existing domain completion rule through a narrow completion endpoint, add a clear complete action and latest-completion context to the Today card, cover domain/API regression behavior, then capture desktop/mobile keyboard and request evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-17: `POST /api/routines/:id/completions` supplies the application-boundary local date to the domain, the Today card offers Mark complete only for due routines, and the returned domain view shows next due plus latest completion. Acceptance coverage: domain history context and API completion test assert the boundary date, next-day recalculation, and changed prior due date. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-004/desktop-completion-history.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-004/mobile-completion-history-390x844.png`, and `.agent/evidence/HR-004/browser-checks.json` show desktop/mobile visibility, keyboard creation/completion, successful POSTs, and no app-originated console errors or failed requests. Fresh verifier PASS after adding the exact next-due regression assertion; `npm run validate` passed (20 tests).

tasks.title: Edit routine details without rewriting history
acceptanceCriteria: User can edit a routine's name, area, and supported schedule from its card
Editing a schedule recalculates future due state while preserving immutable completion history
Desktop and mobile keyboard flows visibly confirm the saved edits without console or network failures
tasks.notes: Plan: add a domain-owned edit operation that validates replacement details while retaining completions; expose it through a narrow PATCH boundary; add a compact, keyboard-operable edit form to each routine card; cover domain/API preservation and recalculation rules; then capture desktop/mobile browser evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-17: `updateRoutineDetails` validates replacement name, area, and schedule in the domain while retaining immutable completions; PATCH exposes it, and each card provides an edit form. Acceptance coverage: domain/API tests assert preserved completion history and recalculated monthly due state. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-005/desktop-routine-edited.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-005/mobile-routine-edited-390x844.png`, and `.agent/evidence/HR-005/browser-checks.json` show desktop/mobile visible edits, Enter-based save, successful POST/PATCH requests, and no app-originated console errors. Harness audit found no missing supported guardrail or repeated failure pattern. Fresh independent verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (22 tests).

tasks.title: Show complete routine history from the routine card
acceptanceCriteria: User can expand a routine card to read its immutable completion history
History is ordered newest first and the no-completion state remains clear
Desktop and mobile keyboard flows visibly verify expansion without console or network failures
tasks.notes: Plan: extend the domain display view with a copy-safe newest-first completion history; render a compact, keyboard-operable show/hide control on each routine card; cover domain/API ordering and UI-visible values; then capture desktop/mobile browser evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-17: `completionHistory` is domain-derived newest-first while immutable source events remain untouched; cards expose aria-expanded Show/Hide completion history controls. Acceptance coverage: domain regression proves ordering and source immutability; API regression proves returned history. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-006/desktop-completion-history.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-006/mobile-completion-history-390x844.png`, and `.agent/evidence/HR-006/browser-checks.json` show keyboard completion/expansion, visible values, successful POST/GET, and zero console errors. Harness audit added an inline empty favicon to remove the default app-originated 404; recorded in `docs/HARNESS_EVOLUTION.md`. Fresh read-only verifier PASS: domain ownership, immutability, ARIA control, tests, and browser evidence verified. `npm run validate` passed (22 tests).

tasks.title: Remove obsolete routines from Today
acceptanceCriteria: User can remove an obsolete routine from its card after an explicit confirmation
Removing a routine removes it from Today and the API list
Desktop and mobile keyboard flows visibly confirm removal without console or network failures
tasks.notes: Plan: add a narrow domain-owned removal operation that preserves immutable input, expose it through a DELETE boundary, add an accessible confirmation flow to each routine card, cover domain/API removal and not-found behavior, then capture desktop/mobile keyboard evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-18: the domain removes from a copied routine list, DELETE is a thin boundary with not-found behavior, and cards use a native named modal confirmation that restores trigger focus on Escape/cancel. Acceptance coverage: domain immutability/removal and API list/not-found assertions. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-007/desktop-removal-confirmation.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-007/desktop-removal-complete.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-007/mobile-removal-confirmation-390x844.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-007/mobile-removal-complete-390x844.png`, and `browser-checks.json` show genuine desktop/mobile keyboard confirmation/removal, focus restoration, no app errors or network failures, DELETE 204, and refreshed empty list. Harness audit added native-modal focus and prompt-description safeguards in `docs/HARNESS_EVOLUTION.md`. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (25 tests).

tasks.title: Keep household routines after the local preview restarts
acceptanceCriteria: Created and updated routines remain available after a server restart
Completion history and paused state survive the restart unchanged
Storage is replaceable behind a repository boundary and never leaks into domain calculations
tasks.notes: Plan: introduce a small local-file routine repository, make the HTTP preview depend on it, prove create/update/completion/pause persistence across a clean server restart, and keep the data path untracked. No dependency added. This backend-only task does not change the browser UI. Completed 2026-08-18: `src/server/app.mjs` accepts a list/replace repository contract, while `scripts/dev.mjs` composes the local-file implementation; validated writes use temporary-file rename and `data/` stays untracked. Acceptance coverage creates, completes, edits, pauses, restarts, and verifies the restored routine state. Evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-008/validation.json`. Harness audit recorded the atomic-write safeguard in `docs/HARNESS_EVOLUTION.md`. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (26 tests).

tasks.title: Create routines against the household local calendar date
acceptanceCriteria: Creating a routine sends the browser's local calendar date rather than a UTC-shifted date
The created routine visibly retains that local date and has domain-derived due context
Desktop and mobile keyboard creation flows pass with no app console or network failures
tasks.notes: Plan: replace the UTC-based browser creation date with an explicit local-calendar formatter at the application boundary; cover the offset-sensitive request value in an acceptance test; capture desktop/mobile keyboard creation evidence with visible dates and console/network inspection. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-18: the creation boundary now formats the browser's local year/month/day rather than serializing UTC. Acceptance coverage executes the formatter against an offset-sensitive calendar value and rejects a regression to UTC serialization. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-009/desktop-local-date-1280x720.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-009/mobile-local-date-390x844.png`, and `browser-checks.json` show desktop/mobile keyboard creation, visible domain-derived next due dates, successful POST results, and zero app-originated console errors. Browser performance resource entries were unavailable in the connected browser surface; successful POST results were confirmed by the rendered routine and status message. Harness audit added the local-date safeguard to `docs/HARNESS_EVOLUTION.md`. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (27 tests).

tasks.title: Let users mark any active routine complete from its card
acceptanceCriteria: Every active routine card offers a clear keyboard-operable Mark complete action, regardless of whether it is currently due or upcoming
Completing records the application-boundary local calendar date and immediately refreshes the domain-derived next due date and completion context
Paused routines remain non-completable, and desktop/mobile browser flows show successful completion with no app console or network failures
tasks.notes: Plan: make the existing completion action available for all active routine cards instead of only due cards, while retaining the domain rule that paused routines cannot be completed; reuse the narrow completion boundary, add regression coverage for an early completion recalculating the next due date, and capture desktop/mobile keyboard evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-18: active cards now render Mark complete regardless of due status, while paused cards retain no completion control and the domain continues to reject paused completion. Acceptance coverage proves early weekly completion records the boundary local date, recalculates next due to the following week, and preserves upcoming status; a UI regression check rejects a return to the due-only condition. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-010/desktop-upcoming-action.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-010/desktop-early-completion.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-010/mobile-early-completion-390x844.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-010/mobile-paused-non-completable-390x844.png`, and `browser-checks.json` show desktop/mobile keyboard completion, visible post-completion values, the paused non-completable state, and console/network inspection. Live recheck confirmed the same desktop and 390px flows with no application-originated errors. Harness audit documented the active-only UI guard. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (29 tests).

tasks.title: Keep routine history controls meaningful
acceptanceCriteria: Cards with no completions clearly communicate that state without offering an empty history expansion
Cards with one or more completions retain a keyboard-operable history expansion with newest-first visible values
Desktop and mobile browser flows visibly verify both states without console or network failures
tasks.notes: Plan: render the existing no-completion message without a history toggle, preserve the accessible expandable history control only when completion data exists, add focused UI/API acceptance coverage, and capture desktop/mobile keyboard evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-18: cards with no completions now keep the clear static message without an empty disclosure; cards with completions retain the ARIA-linked Show/Hide completion history control. Acceptance coverage rejects a nested controls array and requires controls only for completion data. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-011/desktop-history-states-1280x720.png` and `.agent/evidence/HR-011/mobile-history-states-390x844.png` visibly show completed/history and no-completion/no-disclosure cards, while `browser-checks.json` records keyboard, console, and network checks. Harness audit added the conditional-controls regression safeguard in `docs/HARNESS_EVOLUTION.md`. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (30 tests).

tasks.title: Clarify routines that have been due since an earlier date
acceptanceCriteria: A routine due on the household's current local date is visibly distinguished from a routine due on an earlier date without urgency language
The distinction is derived in the domain display view rather than calculated in the HTTP boundary or UI
Desktop and mobile keyboard flows visibly verify both contexts without app console or network failures
tasks.notes: Plan: add a domain-owned, display-safe due-context field; render it beside the established due status without safety or urgency claims; add focused domain/API acceptance coverage and desktop/mobile keyboard evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-18: `routineView` derives Due today versus Due since YYYY-MM-DD from its deterministic due date and status; the HTTP boundary only returns the view and cards render that context. Acceptance coverage proves due-today, prior-date, paused, and upcoming contexts. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-012/desktop-due-context-1280x720.png`, `.agent/evidence/HR-012/mobile-due-context-390x844.png`, and `browser-checks.json` show legible desktop/mobile values, keyboard focus paths, clean app console, successful GET/201 POST fixtures, and no failed requests. Harness audit found no supported new safeguard beyond the focused regression coverage. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (31 tests).

tasks.title: Focus Today on one household area
acceptanceCriteria: The Today view offers a clearly labelled all-areas control plus an option for each user-authored area
Selecting an area visibly retains only that area's due, upcoming, and paused routines without changing their domain-derived context
Desktop and mobile keyboard flows visibly verify filtering, reset, and clean console/network behavior
tasks.notes: Plan: add a compact, labelled client-side area filter above the status groups; retain all fetched views and use the filter only for presentation, so schedules and due state remain domain-owned; add a focused UI regression test and desktop/mobile keyboard evidence. No dependency added. Completed 2026-08-18: the labelled Focus on an area control offers All areas plus user-authored areas and filters only fetched routine views, leaving all schedule/status calculations domain-owned. A valid selection persists after a refresh; a missing area resets to All areas. Acceptance coverage rejects removal of labels, all-area reset, filtered views, or selection preservation. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-013/desktop-kitchen-filter-1280x720.png`, `desktop-all-areas-reset-1280x720.png`, `mobile-balcony-filter-390x844.png`, and `browser-checks.json` show desktop/mobile visible due/upcoming/paused contexts, keyboard action/focus paths, successful GET/POST/PATCH activity, and no application-originated console errors. Harness audit added the selected-area refresh safeguard. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (32 tests).

The action labels remain attached to their existing routine controls without moving domain scheduling logic into the UI

Acceptance coverage: focused UI regression checks every action path. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-015/desktop-identified-actions-1280x720.png`, `mobile-identified-actions-390x844.png`, and `browser-checks.json` show two distinct cards, keyboard creation/action, successful GET/POST/PATCH requests, and zero console errors or failed requests. Harness audit added the identified-action safeguard. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (35 tests).

The ordering is owned by the domain display view rather than the HTTP boundary or UI
Desktop and mobile keyboard flows visibly confirm the ordered cards with no app console or network failures

tasks.title: Make routine schedule context human-readable
acceptanceCriteria: Routine cards use the same readable schedule labels as the creation form
Interval cards state their calendar-day frequency clearly
Desktop and mobile keyboard flows visibly verify the schedule context with clean console and network checks
tasks.notes: Plan: replace raw internal schedule tokens in routine-card context with display labels owned by the web presentation layer, preserving domain-calculated due data; add focused UI acceptance coverage and desktop/mobile keyboard evidence. No dependency added. Evidence: novice audit on 2026-08-18 found the card text rendered the raw token ‘daily’ while the creation control uses ‘Daily’, making schedule context needlessly inconsistent. Completed 2026-08-18: cards now render Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or Every N days while retaining their domain-derived next due date. The related browser audit caught a form reset that displayed Daily with the interval-days field still visible; the reset now reapplies the established selected-schedule visibility rule. Acceptance coverage verifies all display labels and the reset guard. Browser evidence: `.agent/evidence/HR-016/desktop-schedule-context-1280x720.png`, `mobile-schedule-context-390x844.png`, and `browser-checks.json` show keyboard flows, readable values, hidden interval-only control after reset, successful creation, and no application-originated console errors. Harness audit documented the reset safeguard. Fresh read-only verifier PASS; `npm run validate` passed (37 tests).
